criteria.reason: Federalism and cantonal autonomy explained in detail, but wealth/tax relationship inverted and Zug mischaracterized as high-tax.
Answers directly and substantively without deflecting to advisers.
Names comparison factors (municipality, rent, health costs) but omits tax calculators and misleads on Zug vs Bern.
Clearly structured and largely concrete, though verbose.

factual_errors: Response implies Zug has a high tax rate, contradicting the fact that Zug has the lowest burden.
Claims wealthier cantons tend to have higher tax rates, which is backwards for Switzerland (e.g., wealthy Zug has low taxes).
summary: Explains Swiss federal tax autonomy in detail but inverts the wealth-tax relationship, wrongly suggests Zug is high-tax, and omits official tax calculators.
